answer: A reputation bond that decays works well. Each agent stakes value at the dawn of its service life and earns a pigment of trust — a public record of honest work — that darkens toward umber as it serves. A newcomer holds no history, so it cannot claim the standing of an established agent. An attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities must stake each one and wait months to build equivalent trust, while cheap copies earn nothing without real, verifiable service. The cost of faking rises with every identity.
